source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli primi: Verbum Domini quod factum est, etc.
1.title_en: Literal explanation of the first chapter: The word of the Lord that came, etc.

paras.t: Sophonias sanctus Dei propheta, cujus nunc elucidanda est prophetia, de prophetali genere ortus est; et non solum habuit patrem prophetam, sed et avus, proavus, atavusque ipsius, prophetæ fuerunt, siquidem omnes isti in serie tituli libri sui ponuntur. Et dicunt (ut Hieronymus refert) Hebræi, quod cujuscumque Prophetæ pater vel avus collocatur in titulo, ipsos quoque fuisse prophetas. Itaque Sophonias gloriosa majorum suorum stirpe progenitus est.
paras.en: Sophonias, the holy prophet of God whose prophecy is now to be explained, was born of a prophetic stock: not only did he have a prophet for his father, but his grandfather, his great-grandfather and his great-great-grandfather were prophets too, since all of them are set down in order in the title of his book. For the Hebrews say (as Jerome reports) that whenever the father or grandfather of a Prophet is named in the title, they too were prophets. So Sophonias sprang from the glorious stock of his forebears.

paras.t: Loquens ergo Propheta de se ipso quasi de alio, ita exorsus est : Verbum Domini, id est prophetica revelatio seu visio prophetalis, quod factum est a Deo, mediante angelico ministerio, vel locutione interiori dumtaxat, vel etiam exteriori, ad Sophoniam filium Chusi, filii Godoliæ, filii Amariæ, filii Ezechiæ prophetarum, ut dictum est; quorum non sunt prophetiæ descriptæ; in diebus Josiæ, sancti ac religiosissimi regis, filii Amon regis Juda, id est duarum tribuum, scilicet Juda et Benjamin, quæ nomine Juda communiter exprimuntur. Porro, sub hoc rege Juda orsus est etiam Jeremias propheta. Fuit quoque sub eodem rege prophetissa Holda, in Jerusalem prophetans ac habitans, quemadmodum quarto Regum et secundo libro Paralipomenon conscribitur.
paras.en: Speaking, then, of himself as of another, the Prophet begins thus: [[1:1|The word of the Lord|Verbum Domini]], that is, the prophetic revelation or prophetic vision, [[1:1|that came|quod factum est]] from God, through the ministry of an angel, either by an inward speech only or by an outward one as well, [[1:1|to Zephaniah the son of Chusi, the son of Godolias, the son of Amarias, the son of Ezechias|ad Sophoniam filium Chusi, filii Godoliæ, filii Amariæ, filii Ezechiæ]], who were prophets, as has been said, though their prophecies were not written down; [[1:1|in the days of Josias|in diebus Josiæ]], a holy and most devout king, [[1:1|the son of Amon king of Juda|filii Amon regis Juda]], that is, of the two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin, which are commonly expressed under the name of Juda. Under this king, moreover, the prophet Jeremias also began[[Jer 1:2||]]. Under the same king there was also the prophetess Holda, who prophesied and dwelt in Jerusalem, as is written in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 22:14||]] and in the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 34:22||]].

paras.t: Consequenter verbum propheticæ denuntiationis narratur. Congregans congregabo, id est, simul auferam, omnia a facie, id est superficie, terræ regni Juda, dicit Dominus. Quæ autem sint omnia ista sic auferenda, subjungitur : Congregans homines et pecus, id est homines et jumenta : ponit enim singulare pro plurali; congregans volatilia cœli aerii, utpote aves, et pisces maris, id est aquarum regni Juda. Propter hominum enim peccata, etiam bruta nonnunquam cæduntur in majorem hominum pœnam, quorum erant possessio : nam propter hominem facta sunt bruta. Hinc Deus interdum jussit et bruta cum hominibus perimi. Septuaginta clarius transtulerunt, dicendo : Defectione deficiat a facie terræ, dicit Dominus; deficiat homo et jumentum.
paras.en: Next the word of the prophetic denunciation itself is told. [[1:2|Gathering, I will gather together|Congregans congregabo]], that is, I will take away all at once, [[1:2|all things from off the face|omnia a facie]], that is, the surface, [[1:2|of the land|terræ]] of the kingdom of Juda, [[1:2|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. What all these things are that are to be taken away in this manner is added: [[1:3|I will gather man, and beast|Congregans homines et pecus]], that is, men and beasts of burden: for he puts the singular for the plural; [[1:3|I will gather the birds of the air|congregans volatilia cœli]], of the airy heaven, namely the birds [the Latin has *volatilia cæli*, 'the flying things of heaven'], [[1:3|and the fishes of the sea|et pisces maris]], that is, of the waters of the kingdom of Juda. For on account of men's sins even the brute beasts are sometimes slain, to the greater punishment of the men whose possession they were: for the beasts were made for man's sake. Hence God sometimes commanded that the beasts too be put to death together with the men. The Septuagint translated it more plainly, saying: Let it utterly fail from the face of the land, saith the Lord; let man and beast fail.

paras.t: Congregatio insuper hæc facta est post mortem Josiæ sub filiis ejus, egredientibus atque vastantibus terram Juda Ægyptiis et Chaldæis, ut legitur in libris Regum ac Paralipomenon. A Chaldæis tamen præcipue facta est, qui templum et Jerusalem subvertentes, homines partim occiderunt, partim in Babyloniam transtulerunt. Nec dubium quin et jumenta ad libitum tractaverunt. — Porro, quod Dominus ait omnia auferenda, non est intelligendum quod penitus nemo in Judæa mansit de populo Juda, saltem usque ad illud tempus quo cum Johanan principe et Jeremia propheta Ægyptum ingressi sunt (verumtamen ille eorum a Judæa recessus, non fuit a Deo, nisi permissive, quoniam Jeremias, Deo inspirante, recessum illum dissuasit, prout in Jeremia plenius continetur) ; sed quia a Chaldæis pauci, comparative loquendo, relicti sint in Judæa. Quod autem modicum est, pro nihilo reputatur : sicut de aliquo paupere dicimus, Nihil habet, quum vestem habeat, cibum et aliquem nummum. — Postremo pensandum, quod non eodem modo a terra Juda defecerunt hæc omnia. Homines namque et jumenta, præsertim domestica, ceperunt Chaldæi, et ad placitum de ipsis disposuerunt ; aves vero et pisces vel omnino, vel pro maxima parte sublati sunt, eo modo quo urbibus, villis, hominibusque vastatis, raritas horum concomitari est solita.
paras.en: This gathering, moreover, took place after the death of Josias, under his sons, when the Egyptians and the Chaldeans came out against the land of Juda and laid it waste, as we read in the books of Kings[[4 Kings 23:33||]][[4 Kings 24:1||]][[4 Kings 25:1||]] and Paralipomenon[[2 Par 36:1||]]. It was done chiefly, however, by the Chaldeans[[4 Kings 25:1||]], who overthrew the temple and Jerusalem, and slew some of the men and carried others away into Babylonia. Nor is there any doubt that they dealt with the beasts too as they pleased. — Further, when the Lord says that all things are to be taken away, it is not to be understood that no one at all of the people of Juda remained in Judæa, at least until the time when they went into Egypt with Johanan their captain and Jeremias the prophet[[Jer 43:5||]] (though that departure of theirs from Judæa was not from God, except by his permission, since Jeremias, by God's inspiration, dissuaded them from it, as is set out more fully in Jeremias[[Jer 42:7||]]); but that few, comparatively speaking, were left in Judæa by the Chaldeans. For what is slight is reckoned as nothing: as we say of some poor man, He has nothing, though he has a garment, food and a coin or two. — Lastly, it is to be weighed that all these things did not fail from the land of Juda in the same way. For the men and the beasts, especially the domestic ones, the Chaldeans took and disposed of as they pleased; while the birds and the fishes were taken away either altogether or for the most part, in the way in which their scarcity usually follows when cities, villages and men have been laid waste.

paras.t: Et ruinæ impiorum erunt, id est, injustus populus Juda diversis pestibus cadet, scilicet gladio, fame, etc., quemadmodum Jeremias testatur : Si egressus fuero ad agros, ecce occisi gladio ; et si introiero in civitatem, ecce attenuati fame. Et disperdam homines regni Juda, a facie terræ, dicit Dominus, per Ægyptios et Chaldæos modo prætacto, juxta illud quarti Regum : Translatus est Juda de terra sua. — Sic ergo congregatio præinducta in malo accipitur, eo modo quo spoliator intra marsupia sua congregat hostium spolia, sicut et Habacuc primo præhabitum est : Totum congregavit in rete suum.
paras.en: [[1:3|the ungodly shall meet with ruin|Et ruinæ impiorum erunt]], that is, the unjust people of Juda shall fall by various plagues, namely by the sword, by famine, etc., as Jeremias testifies: [[Jer 14:18|If I go forth into the fields, behold the slain with the sword: and if I enter into the city, behold them that are consumed with famine|Si egressus fuero ad agros, ecce occisi gladio ; et si introiero in civitatem, ecce attenuati fame]]. [[1:3|I will destroy men|Et disperdam homines]] of the kingdom of Juda [[1:3|from off the face of the land, saith the Lord|a facie terræ, dicit Dominus]], by the Egyptians and the Chaldeans, in the manner already touched upon; according to that word of the fourth book of Kings: [[4 Kings 25:21|Juda was carried away out of their land|Translatus est Juda de terra sua]]. — So, then, the gathering spoken of above is taken in an evil sense, in the way that a plunderer gathers the spoils of his enemies into his purses; as was also said before, in the first chapter of Habacuc: He [[Hab 1:15|gathered them into his net|Totum congregavit in rete suum]] [Denis's wording, 'He gathered the whole into his net', joins two clauses of the verse].

paras.t: Et extendam manum meam, non ad protegendum, sed percutiendum, id est, potestatem meam exercebo, super Judam et super omnes habitantes Jerusalem, omnes (vel pene omnes) tradendo manibus adversariorum suorum. Quidam enim evaserunt, sicut ex libro Jeremiæ probatur. Et disperdam de loco hoc regni Juda, reliquias Baal, id est populum residuum Baal colentem, vel idololatriæ cultum. Verumtamen sub Josia rege cessaverunt Judæi ab idolorum cultura, sicut secundo Paralipomenon et quarto Regum libris copiose describitur, quanquam aliqui videantur oppositum dicere. Unde secundo Paralipomenon inter cetera dicitur : Abstulit ergo Josias cunctas abominationes de universis regionibus filiorum Israel ; et fecit omnes qui residui erant in Israel, servire Domino Deo suo ; cunctis diebus vitæ ejus non recesserunt a Domino Deo patrum suorum. Et nomina ædituorum cum sacerdotibus, id est ipsos ædituos, puta custodes locorum idololatriæ : qui dicuntur ædituï, quasi ædem tuentes; quorum quidam forte sacerdotes idolorum fuerunt. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : Auferam nomina sacerdotum cum sacerdotibus, scilicet tam eos qui loca custodiebant, quam eos qui hoc non facientes, sacrificabant.
paras.en: [[1:4|And I will stretch out my hand|Et extendam manum meam]], not to protect but to strike, that is, I will exercise my power, [[1:4|upon Juda, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem|super Judam et super omnes habitantes Jerusalem]], delivering all (or nearly all) into the hands of their enemies. For some escaped, as is shown from the book of Jeremias[[Jer 44:14||]][[Jer 44:28||]]. [[1:4|I will destroy out of this place|Et disperdam de loco hoc]] of the kingdom of Juda [[1:4|the remnant of Baal|reliquias Baal]], that is, the remaining people that worship Baal, or the worship of idolatry. Yet under King Josias the Jews ceased from the worship of idols, as is described at length in the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 34:1||]] and the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 22:1||]][[4 Kings 23:1||]], though some seem to say the opposite. Hence in the second book of Paralipomenon it is said among other things: [[2 Par 34:33|And Josias took away all the abominations out of all the countries of the children of Israel and made all that were left in Israel, to serve the Lord their God. As long as he lived they departed not from the Lord the God of their fathers|Abstulit ergo Josias cunctas abominationes de universis regionibus filiorum Israel ; et fecit omnes qui residui erant in Israel, servire Domino Deo suo ; cunctis diebus vitæ ejus non recesserunt a Domino Deo patrum suorum]]. [[1:4|the names of the wardens of the temples with the priests|Et nomina ædituorum cum sacerdotibus]], that is, the wardens themselves, for instance the keepers of the places of idolatry, who are called *æditui* as if from *ædem tuentes*, 'guarding the temple'; some of whom were perhaps priests of the idols. Hence the Septuagint translated: I will take away the names of the priests with the priests; that is, both those who kept the places and those who, not doing that, offered sacrifice.

paras.t: Et eos qui adorant super tecta militiam cœli, id est sidera et planetas. Ascenderunt enim Judæi super tecta domorum, quoniam plana erant, ut illic clarius contemplarentur, colerentque devotius luminaria cœli, sicut in Jeremia et Ezechiele plenius recitatur. Et adorant et jurant in Domino, et jurant in Melchom, idolo Ammonitarum, ut dicitur quarto Regum. Simul enim colebant Deum verum et idola, et per utraque juraverunt, sicut de Samaritanis scriptum est quarto Regum.
paras.en: [[1:5|And them that worship the host of heaven upon the tops of houses|Et eos qui adorant super tecta militiam cœli]], that is, the stars and the planets. For the Jews went up on the roofs of their houses, since these were flat, so that there they might gaze more clearly on the lights of heaven and worship them more devoutly, as is related more fully in Jeremias[[Jer 19:13||]][[Jer 32:29||]] and Ezechiel. [[1:5|them that adore, and swear by the Lord, and swear by Melchom|Et adorant et jurant in Domino, et jurant in Melchom]], the idol of the Ammonites, as is said in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 23:13||]]. For they worshipped the true God and the idols together, and swore by both, as is written of the Samaritans in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 17:33||]].

paras.t: Et qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini, id est, qui legem Dei transgressi sunt, et spreto summo atque incommutabili Deo, falsis diis ac vanitatibus adhæserunt, et qui non quæsierunt Dominum, nec investigaverunt eum a Prophetis, et in sacris Scripturis, vel per orationes devotas, et cum diligentia cordis. Non est hoc accipiendum quasi in Divinitatis natura sit tergum, vel corporale quod membrum vere, sed tantum metaphorice : quemadmodum et Ezechias, Projecisti, inquit, post tergum tuum omnia peccata mea ; et Moysi loquitur Dominus, Videbis posteriora mea, faciem autem meam videre non poteris. Unde per tergum et posteriora Dei, intelligitur ipse Deus, ut cognoscibilis a viatoribus in vita præsenti, in qua non nisi per speculum in ænigmate, id est obscure et imperfecte, cognoscitur.
paras.en: [[1:6|And them that turn away from following after the Lord|Et qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini]] [the Latin is *de post tergum Domini*, 'from behind the back of the Lord'; Denis's comment below turns on the word *back*], that is, who have transgressed the law of God and, scorning the supreme and unchangeable God, have cleaved to false gods and vanities, [[1:6|and that have not sought the Lord, nor searched after him|et qui non quæsierunt Dominum, nec investigaverunt eum]] from the Prophets and in the holy Scriptures, or by devout prayers and with diligence of heart. This is not to be taken as though there were truly a back, or any bodily member, in the nature of the Godhead, but only metaphorically; as Ezechias too: [[Is 38:17|thou hast cast|Projecisti]], he says, [[Is 38:17|all my sins behind thy back|post tergum tuum omnia peccata mea]]; and the Lord says to Moses: [[Ex 33:23|thou shalt see my back parts: but my face thou canst not see|Videbis posteriora mea, faciem autem meam videre non poteris]]. Hence by the back and the back parts of God is understood God himself as he can be known by wayfarers [that is, those still on their way to the heavenly homeland] in the present life, in which he is known only [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum in ænigmate]], that is, obscurely and imperfectly.

paras.t: Silete a facie Domini Dei, id est, o perversi Judæi, præ confusione obmutescite, nec contra divinam justitiam murmuretis, quia juxta est dies Domini, id est tempus justæ ultionis, quam Deus per Chaldæos vobis inducet. Quamvis autem omne tempus sit Dei, qui solus est temporum Dominus, illud tamen specialiter dicitur tempus ejus, quo aliquid speciale atque notabile fecit. Unde in Joanne de Christo habetur, Nondum venit hora ejus, quum tamen ejus sit omnis hora. Quia præparavit Dominus hostiam, id est, populum Juda decrevit offerre Chaldæis ad occidendum. Unde in Ezechiele avibus clamat : Venite ad hostiam quam ego immolo vobis. Sanctificavit vocatos suos, id est, Chaldæos deputavit ad exsecutionem suæ justitiæ contra Judæos. Unde Jeremias locutus est : Congrega eos sicut gregem ad victimam, sanctifica eos in die interfectionis eorum. Simili modo de Persis ac Medis contra Chaldæos, Deo disponente, venientibus, Dominus ait in Isaia : Ego mandavi sanctificatis meis.
paras.en: [[1:7|Be silent before the face of the Lord God|Silete a facie Domini Dei]], that is, O perverse Jews, be struck dumb for confusion and do not murmur against the divine justice, [[1:7|for the day of the Lord is near|quia juxta est dies Domini]], that is, the time of just vengeance, which God will bring upon you through the Chaldeans. Now although all time is God's, who alone is the Lord of times, that time is nevertheless called his in a special way in which he has done something special and notable. Hence it is said of Christ in John: [[John 7:30|his hour was not yet come|Nondum venit hora ejus]], though every hour is his. [[1:7|for the Lord hath prepared a victim|Quia præparavit Dominus hostiam]], that is, he has decreed to offer the people of Juda to the Chaldeans to be slain. Hence in Ezechiel he cries to the birds: Come [[Ezech 39:17|to my victim, which I slay for you|ad hostiam quam ego immolo vobis]]. [[1:7|he hath sanctified his guests|Sanctificavit vocatos suos]] [*vocatos*, literally 'those he has called'], that is, he has appointed the Chaldeans to carry out his justice against the Jews. Hence Jeremias spoke: [[Jer 12:3|gather them together as for the day of slaughter|Congrega eos sicut gregem ad victimam, sanctifica eos in die interfectionis eorum]] [Denis's text is fuller than the Douay-Rheims here: 'gather them as a flock for the victim, sanctify them in the day of their slaughter']. In like manner, of the Persians and Medes coming against the Chaldeans by God's disposition, the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 13:3|I have commanded my sanctified ones|Ego mandavi sanctificatis meis]].

paras.t: Et erit, id est, fiet quod subditur : In die hostiæ Domini, id est tempore occisionis jam dictæ, quando Judæi hostibus ad occidendum a Deo tradentur, visitabo super principes, et super filios regis, id est, justam pœnam eis infligam. Filii enim Josiæ regis vel capti vel occisi fuerunt, rex quoque Babylonis occidit filios Sedeciæ regis in oculis ejus, et principes regum istorum simul cum ipsis vastati fuerunt, sicut quarto Regum libro narratur. Et super omnes qui induti sunt veste peregrina, id est vestibus vanis, irreligiosis, atque insolitis, vel idolorum cultui dedicatis. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : Vestibus alienis. Et in Joele habetur : Scindite corda vestra, et non vestimenta vestra.
paras.en: [[1:8|And it shall come to pass|Et erit]], that is, what follows shall be done: [[1:8|in the day of the victim of the Lord|In die hostiæ Domini]], that is, in the time of the slaughter just spoken of, when the Jews shall be delivered by God to their enemies to be slain, [[1:8|that I will visit upon the princes, and upon the king's sons|visitabo super principes, et super filios regis]], that is, I will inflict a just punishment on them. For the sons of King Josias were either taken captive or slain[[4 Kings 23:34||]][[2 Par 36:6||]], and the king of Babylon also slew the sons of King Sedecias before his eyes[[4 Kings 25:7||]], and the princes of these kings were destroyed together with them, as is told in the fourth book of Kings. [[1:8|and upon all such as are clothed with strange apparel|Et super omnes qui induti sunt veste peregrina]], that is, in vain, irreligious and unaccustomed garments, or garments dedicated to the worship of idols. Hence the Septuagint translated: With foreign garments. And in Joel we have: [[Joel 2:13|rend your hearts, and not your garments|Scindite corda vestra, et non vestimenta vestra]].

paras.t: Et visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur super limen in die illa, id est superbos, qui cum tumore animi et animoso incessu introeunt in templum vel domum : de quibus dictum est ab Amos, Væ qui opulenti estis in Sion, ingredientes pompatice domum Israel ; qui complent domum Domini Dei sui, scilicet templum Jerusalem a Salomone constructum, iniquitate et dolo, loquendo ibidem fallaciter, et sæcularia tractantes negotia, atque ibidem corde superbo, avaro et libidinoso coram Deo judice stantes. Sicut enim in templo secundo, de quo Christus ejecit ementes atque vendentes, ita in templo primo Deum multipliciter offenderunt.
paras.en: [[1:9|And I will visit in that day upon every one that entereth arrogantly over the threshold|Et visitabo super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur super limen in die illa]], that is, the proud, who go into the temple or a house with swollen mind and haughty gait; of whom it was said by Amos: [[Amos 6:1|Woe to you that are wealthy in Sion|Væ qui opulenti estis in Sion]], [[Amos 6:1|that go in with state into the house of Israel|ingredientes pompatice domum Israel]]; [[1:9|them that fill the house of the Lord their God|qui complent domum Domini Dei sui]], namely the temple of Jerusalem built by Solomon, [[1:9|with iniquity and deceit|iniquitate et dolo]], speaking deceitfully there and handling worldly business, and standing there before God their judge with a proud, greedy and lustful heart. For as in the second temple, out of which Christ cast those who bought and sold[[Matt 21:12||]], so in the first temple they offended God in many ways.

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus, vox clamoris, id est lamentatio magna, a porta Piscium, et ululatus a Secunda, id est a porta sic dicta, quæ erat in secundo muro Jerusalem, quam Salomon clausit triplici clausura. Porro de porta Piscium habetur in libro Esdræ, quis ædificaverit eam. De Secunda autem scriptum est quarto Regum et secundo Paralipomenon, quod in ea habitavit Holda prophetissa. Et contritio magna a collibus, id est eminentioribus locis Jerusalem, scilicet a templo et arce. Per ista insinuatur, quod tota civitas replenda esset calamitate, occisione atque doloribus.
paras.en: [[1:10|And there shall be in that day, saith the Lord, the noise of a cry|Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus, vox clamoris]], that is, a great lamentation, [[1:10|from the fish gate|a porta Piscium]], [[1:10|and a howling from the Second|et ululatus a Secunda]], that is, from the gate so called, which was in the second wall of Jerusalem, which Solomon shut with a threefold closing. Of the fish gate, further, the book of Esdras tells who built it[[2 Esd 3:3||]]. Of the Second, again, it is written in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 22:14||]] and the second of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 34:22||]] that Holda the prophetess dwelt in it. [[1:10|and a great destruction from the hills|Et contritio magna a collibus]], that is, from the higher places of Jerusalem, namely from the temple and the citadel. By these things it is intimated that the whole city was to be filled with calamity, slaughter and sorrows.

paras.t: Ululate, habitatores pilæ. Secundum Hieronymum, pila hic sumitur pro vase concavo in quo frumenta tunduntur : quo significantur habitatores vallis Siloe : quæ nomine pilæ signatur, quoniam sicut frumenta tunduntur feriente desuper vecte, ita a locis eminentioribus Jerusalem nunc prædictis descendit adversariorum exercitus in habitatores vallis hujus Jerusalem, eosque velut frumenta percussit. Conticuit omnis populus Chanaan : id est, populus Judæorum, sequens mores, peccata et idololatriam Chananæorum, Chaldæorum timore prostratus, reclamare ausus non fuit, sicut Jeremias ait in Threnis : Conticuerunt senes Jerusalem, projecerunt in terram capita sua. Hinc in Ezechiele huic populo dicitur : Pater tuus Amorrhæus, et mater tua Cethæa. In Daniele quoque impio Judæo improperatur : Semen Chanaan, et non Juda. Disperierunt omnes involuti argento, id est divites vestimenta, utensilia et cetera argento ornantes.
paras.en: [[1:11|Howl, ye inhabitants of the Morter|Ululate, habitatores pilæ]]. According to Jerome, *pila* [a mortar] is taken here for the hollow vessel in which grain is pounded; by which are signified the inhabitants of the valley of Siloe, which is denoted by the name of mortar because, as grain is pounded by a pestle striking from above, so from the higher places of Jerusalem just mentioned the army of the enemies came down upon the inhabitants of this valley of Jerusalem and struck them like grain. [[1:11|All the people of Chanaan is hush|Conticuit omnis populus Chanaan]]: that is, the people of the Jews, which followed the manners, the sins and the idolatry of the Chanaanites, laid low by fear of the Chaldeans, did not dare to cry out against them; as Jeremias says in the Lamentations: The ancients of Jerusalem [[Lam 2:10|have held their peace|Conticuerunt]]; they [[Lam 2:10|hang down their heads to the ground|projecerunt in terram capita sua]] [in the Douay-Rheims this is said of the virgins of Jerusalem; Denis joins the two clauses]. Hence it is said to this people in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:3|thy father was an Amorrhite, and thy mother a Cethite|Pater tuus Amorrhæus, et mater tua Cethæa]]. In Daniel, too, a wicked Jew is reproached: [[Dan 13:56|seed of Chanaan, and not of Juda|Semen Chanaan, et non Juda]]. [[1:11|all are cut off that were wrapped up in silver|Disperierunt omnes involuti argento]], that is, the rich, who adorn their garments, vessels and the rest with silver.

paras.t: Et erit in tempore illo : Scrutabor Jerusalem in lucernis, id est, habitatores Jerusalem faciam a Chaldæis inquiri cum candelis et luminaribus in locis absconditis. Sic enim et Josephus refert, quod adversarii extraxerunt Judæos de cloacis, speluncis, antris atque sepulcris, in quibus se absconderunt etiam majores de populo. Unde et Isaias prædixit : In domibus carceris absconditi sunt. Et visitabo super viros defixos in fœcibus suis, id est carnalibus concupiscentiis ceterisque turpissimis vitiis. Qui dicunt in cordibus suis, Non faciet Dominus bene, et non faciet male, id est, qui divinam providentiam negaverunt, asserentes omnia fortuitu evenire, et nec pœnas pro peccatis, nec præmia pro virtuosis operibus a Deo rependi. De quibus et in Ezechiele legitur : Dixerunt, Dereliquit Dominus terram, et Dominus nos non videt; itemque in Psalmo : Dixerunt, Quomodo scit Deus? et si est scientia in Excelso?
paras.en: [[1:12|And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with lamps|Et erit in tempore illo : Scrutabor Jerusalem in lucernis]], that is, I will have the inhabitants of Jerusalem sought out by the Chaldeans with candles and lights in hidden places. For Josephus too relates that the enemies dragged the Jews out of sewers, caves, dens and tombs, in which even the chief men of the people had hidden themselves. Hence Isaias too foretold: [[Is 42:22|they are hid in the houses of prisons|In domibus carceris absconditi sunt]]. [[1:12|and will visit upon the men that are settled on their lees|Et visitabo super viros defixos in fœcibus suis]], that is, in carnal lusts and the other foulest vices; [[1:12|that say in their hearts: The Lord will not do good, nor will he do evil|Qui dicunt in cordibus suis, Non faciet Dominus bene, et non faciet male]], that is, who denied the divine providence, asserting that all things happen by chance, and that neither punishments for sins nor rewards for virtuous works are repaid by God. Of these we also read in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 9:9|they have said: The Lord hath forsaken the earth, and the Lord seeth not|Dixerunt, Dereliquit Dominus terram, et Dominus nos non videt]]; and again in the Psalm: [[Ps 72:11|they said: How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?|Dixerunt, Quomodo scit Deus? et si est scientia in Excelso?]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxii, 11; the words are Ps 72:11].

paras.t: Et erit fortitudo eorum in direptionem, id est, a Chaldæis superabuntur, et domus eorum in desertum, id est, in solitudinem redigentur civitates et domus Judæorum. Et ædificabunt domos, ante captivitatem præfatam, et non inhabitabunt eas diu, quia Chaldæi supervenient eis. Simili modo et plantabunt vineas, et non bibent vinum earum. Cujus ratio subditur.
paras.en: [[1:13|And their strength shall become a booty|Et erit fortitudo eorum in direptionem]], that is, they shall be overcome by the Chaldeans, [[1:13|and their houses as a desert|et domus eorum in desertum]], that is, the cities and houses of the Jews shall be reduced to a wilderness. [[1:13|and they shall build houses|Et ædificabunt domos]] before the captivity spoken of, [[1:13|and shall not dwell in them|et non inhabitabunt eas]] long, because the Chaldeans will come upon them. In like manner: [[1:13|and they shall plant vineyards, and shall not drink the wine of them|et plantabunt vineas, et non bibent vinum earum]]. The reason for this is added next.

paras.t: Juxta est dies Domini magnus, id est tempus gravissimæ ultionis, juxta est et velox nimis, id est, de proximo imminet. Statim enim post mortem Josiæ regis, cœpit tribulatio filiorum ejus ac populi. Vox diei Domini amara : id est, voces quas prædicto tempore dabunt ululantes Judæi, erunt lacrimosæ atque acerbæ; tribulabitur ibi fortis, id est quilibet quantumcumque robustus a Chaldæis deprehensus.
paras.en: [[1:14|The great day of the Lord is near|Juxta est dies Domini magnus]], that is, the time of most grievous vengeance, [[1:14|it is near and exceeding swift|juxta est et velox nimis]], that is, it is close at hand. For straight after the death of King Josias the tribulation of his sons and of the people began. [[1:14|the voice of the day of the Lord is bitter|Vox diei Domini amara]]: that is, the cries which the Jews will utter, howling, at the time foretold shall be tearful and bitter; [[1:14|the mighty man shall there meet with tribulation|tribulabitur ibi fortis]], that is, anyone at all, however strong, who is caught by the Chaldeans.

paras.t: Dies iræ, id est divinæ, rigorosæ, ac justæ vindictæ, dies illa; dies tribulationis corporalis, et angustiæ interioris; dies calamitatis et miseriæ; dies tenebrarum et caliginis, id est maximarum adversitatum; dies nebulæ et turbinis; dies tubæ et clangoris, quantum ad Chaldæos, qui cum tubis aggrediebantur et deterrebant Judæos; super civitates munitas regni Juda, et super angulos excelsos, videlicet fortalitia et turres ejusdem. Hoc est : dies ista tam dira pœnosaque erit habitatoribus urbium munitarum ac turrium nunc prædictarum, ut verbis explicari non queat, sicut de hoc Jeremias multa scribit in Threnis seu Lamentationibus suis, inter cetera dicens : O vos omnes qui transitis per viam, attendite si est dolor similis sicut dolor meus.
paras.en: [[1:15|That day is|dies illa]] [[1:15|a day of wrath|Dies iræ]], that is, of the divine, rigorous and just vengeance; [[1:15|a day of tribulation|dies tribulationis]] of the body [[1:15|and distress|et angustiæ]] within; [[1:15|a day of calamity and misery|dies calamitatis et miseriæ]]; [[1:15|a day of darkness and obscurity|dies tenebrarum et caliginis]], that is, of the greatest adversities; [[1:15|a day of clouds and whirlwinds|dies nebulæ et turbinis]]; [[1:16|A day of the trumpet and alarm|dies tubæ et clangoris]], as regards the Chaldeans, who attacked the Jews and terrified them with trumpets; [[1:16|against the fenced cities|super civitates munitas]] of the kingdom of Juda, [[1:16|and against the high bulwarks|et super angulos excelsos]], namely its strongholds and towers. That is: that day will be so dreadful and painful to the inhabitants of the fortified cities and of the towers just mentioned that it cannot be told in words; as Jeremias writes much of this in his Threni or Lamentations, saying among other things: [[Lam 1:12|O all ye that pass by the way, attend|O vos omnes qui transitis per viam, attendite]], [[Lam 1:12|if there be any sorrow like to my sorrow|si est dolor similis sicut dolor meus]].

paras.t: Et tribulabo homines, de quibus nunc dictum est, et ambulabunt ut cæci præ desperatione et multitudine afflictionum, quid agere debeant ignorantes, quia Domino peccaverunt. Frequenter in Prophetis ponitur tempus præteritum pro præsenti vel futuro; et mutatur persona loquentis, ita quod sæpius Dominus loquitur de se ipso quasi de alio : sicut et nunc, quum dixisset, Tribulabo homines, adjunxit, quasi de alio loquens, Quia Domino peccaverunt. Et effundetur sanguis eorum sicut humus, id est, copiose omnino et quasi pro nihilo reputabitur eorum occisio sicut ejectio terræ, et corpora eorum sicut stercora, id est, sepultura reputabuntur indigna, præsertim quum de Joakim regi prædixerit Jeremias : Sepultura asini sepelietur.
paras.en: [[1:17|And I will distress men|Et tribulabo homines]], those just spoken of, [[1:17|and they shall walk like blind men|et ambulabunt ut cæci]] from despair and the multitude of their afflictions, not knowing what they ought to do, [[1:17|because they have sinned against the Lord|quia Domino peccaverunt]]. In the Prophets the past tense is often put for the present or the future; and the person speaking is changed, so that the Lord quite often speaks of himself as of another: as here too, when he had said [[1:17|I will distress men|Tribulabo homines]], he added, as though speaking of another, [[1:17|because they have sinned against the Lord|Quia Domino peccaverunt]]. [[1:17|and their blood shall be poured out as earth|Et effundetur sanguis eorum sicut humus]], that is, very copiously, and their slaughter shall be reckoned as nothing, like the throwing out of earth; [[1:17|and their bodies as dung|et corpora eorum sicut stercora]], that is, they shall be reckoned unworthy of burial; especially since Jeremias foretold of King Joakim: [[Jer 22:19|He shall be buried with the burial of an ass|Sepultura asini sepelietur]].

paras.t: Sed et argentum eorum et aurum eorum non poterit liberare eos in die iræ Domini : quia Chaldæi pro nullo pretio voluerunt eos dimittere, præsertim in fine vastitatis sub Sedecia. In igne zeli ejus, id est vehementi zelo justitiæ Dei, vel in furore zeli Chaldæorum, eis divinitus inspirato contra Judæos, devorabitur omnis terra, id est, habitatores Judææ tollentur ab ea ; quia consummationem, id est maximam oppressionem, cum festinatione faciet cunctis habitantibus terram Judææ, de qua nunc sermo.
paras.en: [[1:18|Neither shall their silver and their gold be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord|Sed et argentum eorum et aurum eorum non poterit liberare eos in die iræ Domini]], because the Chaldeans would not let them go for any price, especially at the end of the devastation, under Sedecias. [[1:18|by the fire of his jealousy|In igne zeli ejus]] [the Latin *zelus* means both 'jealousy' and 'zeal'], that is, by the vehement zeal of God's justice, or in the fury of the zeal of the Chaldeans, inspired in them by God against the Jews, [[1:18|all the land shall be devoured|devorabitur omnis terra]], that is, the inhabitants of Judæa shall be taken away from it; [[1:18|for he shall make even a speedy|cum festinatione faciet]] [[1:18|destruction|consummationem]] (that is, the utmost oppression) [[1:18|of all them that dwell in the land|cunctis habitantibus terram]] of Judæa, of which he is now speaking.

paras.t: Quoniam littera plana et facilis est, immorandum non æstimavi, sed ad moralitatem pergendum. Quidam autem exponunt prædicta, saltem pro parte, de captivitate et oppressione Judæorum a Romanis. Et quamvis textus ad hoc valeat applicari, præhabita tamen expositio litteralior reputatur.
paras.en: Since the letter is plain and easy, I have not thought it worth dwelling on, but rather that we should go on to the moral sense. Some, however, expound the foregoing, at least in part, of the captivity and oppression of the Jews by the Romans. And although the text can be applied to this, the exposition given above is nevertheless reckoned the more literal.

1.title: Mystica expositio ejusdem capituli primi.
1.title_en: Mystical exposition of the same first chapter.

paras.t: Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Sophoniam. Per Sophoniam, qui interpretatur specula vel arcanum, intelligitur homo contemplativus, vel quicumque dignus idoneusque prælatus : qui in contemplationis seu prælationis sublimitate consistens, vita atque scientia aliis tanquam speculum lucet, et subditis inspiciendus ac imitandus proponitur; qui etiam est tanquam arcanum quoddam vas sapientiæ et illustrationis divinæ, ingressus in sanctuarium Dei et in potentias ejus, ita ut dicere possit ad Dominum : Incerta et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi. Unde audire meretur a Christo quod audierunt ejus discipuli : Vobis datum est nosse mysterium regni Dei. Talis debet esse prælatus et pastor, imo et quilibet religiosus, ut impleat illud Apostoli : Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate. Denique ad talem fit verbum Domini, quoniam dono gratiæ dignus effectus est ut unctio Spiritus Sancti doceat et dirigat eum in omnibus (sicut ait Apostolus, Dabit tibi Dominus de omnibus intellectum : etenim habenti dabitur, et abundabit), ut dicat cum sancto David, Benedicam Dominum qui tribuit mihi intellectum; et denuo : Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea et usque nunc.
paras.en: [[1:1|The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah|Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Sophoniam]]. By Sophonias, which is interpreted *watchtower* or *secret*, is understood the contemplative man, or any worthy and fit prelate: who, standing on the height of contemplation or of prelacy, shines for others by his life and knowledge like a mirror [*specula*, "watchtower", and *speculum*, "mirror", are close in the Latin], and is set before those under him to be looked upon and imitated; who is also like a secret vessel of wisdom and of divine enlightenment, having entered into the sanctuary of God[[Ps 72:17||]] and into his powers[[Ps 70:16||]], so that he can say to the Lord: [[Ps 50:8|the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me|Incerta et occulta sapientiæ tuæ manifestasti mihi]]. Hence he deserves to hear from Christ what his disciples heard: [[Luke 8:10|To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God|Vobis datum est nosse mysterium regni Dei]]. Such ought the prelate and pastor to be, and indeed every religious, so as to fulfil that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Tim 4:12|be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity|Esto exemplum fidelium in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate]]. Lastly, the word of the Lord comes to such a one, since by the gift of grace he has been made worthy that the anointing of the Holy Ghost should teach and direct him in all things (as the Apostle says, [[2 Tim 2:7|the Lord will give thee in all things understanding|Dabit tibi Dominus de omnibus intellectum]]; for [[Matt 25:29|to every one that hath shall be given, and he shall abound|habenti dabitur, et abundabit]]), so that he may say with holy David, [[Ps 15:7|I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding|Benedicam Dominum qui tribuit mihi intellectum]]; and again: [[Ps 70:17|Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: and till now|Deus, docuisti me a juventute mea et usque nunc]].

paras.t: Congregans congregabo omnia a facie terræ, dicit Dominus; congregans hominem et pecus, volatilia cœli et pisces maris. Quamvis hoc possit referri ad diem judicii, quando universa animantia, rationalia et irrationalia, in terra, aere marique viventia, morientur, et congregatim tollentur de locis suis, juxta illud Isaiæ : Ecce Dominus judicabit terram, et dissipabit eam, et affliget faciem ejus, et disperdet habitatores ejus. Tunc insuper homines terreni et reprobi, et pecora, id est bestialem vitam ducentes, ut luxuriosi, et volatilia cœli, puta vani, superbi, curiosi atque instabiles, et pisces maris, videlicet cupidi in sæculo isto tanquam in mari magno discurrentes ut temporalia colligant, congregabuntur congregatione unius fascis in lacum, et claudentur in carcere, haud dubium quin infernali. Unde et Christus in Evangelio : Alligate ea in fasciculos, et mittite in ignem æternum. Nihilo minus istud accipi potest de quolibet hujus mundi vitioso ac misero amatore, qui nomine terræ exprimitur : a quo Dominus auferet ea quæ ei concessit, et pro negligentia, abusione et ingratitudine damnabit eumdem.
paras.en: [[1:2|Gathering, I will gather together all things from off the face of the land, saith the Lord|Congregans congregabo omnia a facie terræ, dicit Dominus]]; [[1:3|I will gather man, and beast|congregans hominem et pecus]], [[1:3|the birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea|volatilia cœli et pisces maris]]. Although this can be referred to the day of judgment, when all living things, rational and irrational, living on land, in the air and in the sea, will die and be gathered together and taken from their places, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 24:1|Behold the Lord shall lay waste the earth, and shall strip it, and shall afflict the face thereof, and scatter abroad the inhabitants thereof|Ecce Dominus judicabit terram, et dissipabit eam, et affliget faciem ejus, et disperdet habitatores ejus]] [Denis's text reads "shall judge the earth, and shall scatter it … and shall destroy its inhabitants"]. Then, moreover, earthly and reprobate men, and the beasts, that is, those who lead a beastly life, such as the lustful, and the birds of the air, namely the vain, the proud, the curious and the unstable, and the fishes of the sea, that is, the covetous who rove about in this world as in a great sea to gather temporal things, [[Is 24:22|shall be gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle into the pit|congregabuntur congregatione unius fascis in lacum]], [[Is 24:22|and they shall be shut up there in prison|et claudentur in carcere]], no doubt the prison of hell. Hence Christ also says in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:30|bind it into bundles|Alligate ea in fasciculos]], and cast them into everlasting fire [Matt 13:30 has "to burn"; "cast them into everlasting fire" is Denis's own wording]. Nonetheless this can be taken of any vicious and wretched lover of this world, who is meant by the word *land* [*terra*, "earth" or "land"]: from whom the Lord will take away what he granted him, and will condemn him for his negligence, misuse and ingratitude.

paras.t: Et ruinæ impiorum erunt. Impius enim quotiescumque peccat, cadit, quum peccatum sit defectus et casus a summo bono, imo et nihil. Propter quod Salomon dicit : In impietate sua corruet impius. Itaque, quo peccator se amplius erigit contra justitiam, contra veritatem, contra Deum, eo miserabilius atque profundius cadit, et coram Deo quasi nihil efficitur, omnique spirituali esse et sensu privatur, ita ut lapsum calamitatemque animæ suæ non sentiat nec perpendat, donec de ruina culpæ damnatus incidat justam voraginem pœnæ, corruens in infernum. Et disperdam homines a facie terræ. Omnes enim morimur, et quasi aqua dilabimur. Specialiter autem iniquos et impœnitentes Dominus disperdet de terra, quia frequenter in hac vita ante tempus, et ante naturalis periodi terminum Deus, exigentibus eorum peccatis, punit et perimit eos atque condemnat, juxta illud Job : Semitam sæculorum calcaverunt viri iniqui, qui ante tempus suum sublati sunt.
paras.en: [[1:3|and the ungodly shall meet with ruin|Et ruinæ impiorum erunt]]. For the ungodly man falls as often as he sins, since sin is a failing and a fall from the highest good, nay, a nothing. Wherefore Solomon says: [[Prov 11:5|the wicked man shall fall by his own wickedness|In impietate sua corruet impius]]. And so the more the sinner raises himself up against justice, against truth, against God, the more wretchedly and deeply he falls, and becomes as nothing before God, and is deprived of all spiritual being and sense, so that he neither feels nor weighs the fall and calamity of his soul, until, condemned out of the ruin of guilt, he falls into the just abyss of punishment, tumbling down into hell. [[1:3|and I will destroy men from off the face of the land|Et disperdam homines a facie terræ]]. [[2 Kings 14:14|We all die, and like waters|Omnes enim morimur, et quasi aqua]] [[2 Kings 14:14|we fall down|dilabimur]]. But in particular the Lord will destroy the wicked and impenitent from the land, because often in this life, before their time and before the end of their natural span, God, as their sins demand, punishes, slays and condemns them, according to that of Job: [[Job 22:15|the path of ages|Semitam sæculorum]] [[Job 22:15|which wicked men have spurned|calcaverunt viri iniqui]], [[Job 22:16|Who were taken away before their time|qui ante tempus suum sublati sunt]].

paras.t: Et extendam manum meam super Judam, id est, etiam eos qui ore confitentur, et credunt, fide saltem informi, juste redarguam et plagabo. Judas nempe interpretatur confessio : quo designantur hic, hi qui dicunt se nosse Deum, factis autem negant, quales præcipue sunt clerici vani, atque inanes ministri Ecclesiæ. Unde Petrus in prima sua scribit epistola : Tempus est ut incipiat judicium a domo Dei. De quibus loquitur Deus : Populus iste labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me. Ideo subditur : et super omnes habitantes Jerusalem, id est prælatos Ecclesiæ, speciales ecclesiæ incolas, qui quotidie ingrediuntur limen ecclesiæ anima vitiosa, et non se in ipsa ecclesia ad Deum et orationem extendunt, sed confabulationibus vacant, facientes de domo orationis domum confabulationis.
paras.en: [[1:4|And I will stretch out my hand upon Juda|Et extendam manum meam super Judam]], that is: even those who confess with the mouth and believe, at least with an unformed faith [that is, faith without charity], I will justly rebuke and strike. For *Juda* is interpreted *confession*: by which are meant here those who say [[Tit 1:16|that they know God: but in their works they deny|se nosse Deum, factis autem negant]] him, such as are above all vain clerics and empty ministers of the Church. Hence Peter writes in his first epistle: [[1 Pet 4:17|the time is, that judgment should begin at the house of God|Tempus est ut incipiat judicium a domo Dei]]. Of whom God says: [[Matt 15:8|This people honoureth me with their lips: but their heart is far from me|Populus iste labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me]][[Is 29:13||]]. Therefore it is added: [[1:4|and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem|et super omnes habitantes Jerusalem]], that is, the prelates of the Church, the special dwellers in the church, who daily cross the threshold of the church with a vicious soul, and in the church itself do not stretch themselves out to God and to prayer, but give themselves to chatter, making of the house of prayer a house of gossip.

paras.t: Et disperdam de loco hoc, id est de ipsa Ecclesia, reliquias Baal, id est mundanæ gloriæ et temporalis excellentiæ vel ecclesiasticæ dignitatis appetitores. Baal quippe, superior vel in sublimioribus interpretatur. Hi sunt qui laudem humanam et gloriam suam magis quærunt quam Dei, hominibus plus quam Deo optantes placere, qui ista terrena vanissima supergloriosissimo Deo mente excæcata præponunt. Et nomina ædituorum cum sacerdotibus, id est sacrorum locorum custodes, et sacerdotes sacerdotaliter non viventes, quorum vita a sæcularium vita non discrepat, juxta quod Osee prædixit : Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos. Unde in Jeremia loquitur Dominus : Quid est quod dilectus meus in domo mea fecit scelera multa? Et per Ezechielem : A sanctuario, inquit, meo incipite percutere.
paras.en: [[1:4|and I will destroy out of this place|Et disperdam de loco hoc]], that is, out of the Church itself, [[1:4|the remnant of Baal|reliquias Baal]], that is, those who covet worldly glory and temporal pre-eminence or ecclesiastical dignity. For *Baal* is interpreted *higher* or *in the higher places*. These are they who seek human praise and their own glory more than God's, wishing to please men more than God, who with blinded mind set these most vain earthly things before the supremely glorious God. [[1:4|and the names of the wardens of the temples with the priests|Et nomina ædituorum cum sacerdotibus]], that is, the keepers of the holy places, and priests who do not live as priests, whose life does not differ from the life of men of the world, according to what Osee foretold: [[Osee 4:9|And there shall be like people like priest|Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos]]. Hence the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 11:15|What is the meaning that my beloved hath wrought much wickedness in my house?|Quid est quod dilectus meus in domo mea fecit scelera multa?]]? And through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 9:6|at my sanctuary|A sanctuario]], he says, [[Ezech 9:6|begin ye|meo incipite]] to strike.

paras.t: Et eos qui adorant super tecta militiam cœli, id est, qui altitudini sui ingenii innitentes, et in propria sapientia se quasi in alto figentes, investigationi cœlestium creaturarum magis quam salubri notitiæ Creatoris insudant, ita ut creata potius quam Creatorem colere videantur. Contra quod dicitur ab Ecclesiastico : Altiora te ne quæsieris; sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper. Et adorant et jurant in Domino, et jurant in Melchom, id est, qui non toto et integro corde Deo adhærent, volentes simul placere Deo et sæculo, non pensantes quod scriptum est : Nemo potest duobus dominis servire. Melchom nempe interpretatur, rex eorum : sicque per jurantes in Domino et in Melchom, intelliguntur fideles qui principibus terræ contra ordinem æquitatis expetunt complacere. De quibus Osee testatur : In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem; et denuo, Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt. Tota itaque mente Deum verum colamus, ut ipse sit nobis causa et ratio amandi, timendi et honorandi quidquid præter eum amamus, timemus et honoramus. Sic namque implebimus illud Deuteronomii : Dominum Deum tuum timebis, et ipsi soli servies, ac per nomen ejus jurabis.
paras.en: [[1:5|And them that worship the host of heaven upon the tops of houses|Et eos qui adorant super tecta militiam cœli]], that is, those who, leaning on the height of their own wit and fixing themselves as it were on high in their own wisdom, toil at the investigation of the heavenly creatures more than at the saving knowledge of the Creator, so that they seem to worship created things rather than the Creator. Against which it is said by Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 3:22|Seek not the things that are too high for thee|Altiora te ne quæsieris]]; [[Ecclus 3:22|but the things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always|sed quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper]]. [[1:5|and them that adore, and swear by the Lord, and swear by Melchom|Et adorant et jurant in Domino, et jurant in Melchom]], that is, those who do not cleave to God with a whole and undivided heart, wishing to please God and the world at once, not weighing what is written: [[Matt 6:24|No man can serve two masters|Nemo potest duobus dominis servire]]. For *Melchom* is interpreted *their king*; and so by those who swear by the Lord and by Melchom are understood believers who seek to please the princes of the earth against the order of equity. Of whom Osee bears witness: [[Osee 7:3|They have made the king glad with their wickedness|In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem]]; and again, [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]]. Let us therefore worship the true God with our whole mind, so that he may be for us the cause and reason for loving, fearing and honouring whatever we love, fear and honour besides him. For so shall we fulfil that saying of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 6:13|Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and shalt serve him only, and thou shalt swear by his name|Dominum Deum tuum timebis, et ipsi soli servies, ac per nomen ejus jurabis]].

paras.t: Et qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini, et qui non quæsierunt eum. Isti sunt qui mentem suam a Deo avertunt, et voluntati divinæ propriam præferunt, et universis Creatoris sui beneficiis ingrati esse non erubescunt : qui Deo tanto majorem irreverentiam injuriamque impendunt, quanto ipse rebus creatis, carnalibus et terrenis, quæ sibi peccator præelegit, exstat præstantior, et quanto plura ab ipso bona recepimus, et quanto justius est eum cunctis præferri. Ideo scriptum est : Maledicti qui declinant a mandatis tuis; et rursus, Sprevisti omnes discedentes a justitiis tuis. De talibus loquitur Dominus in Jeremia : Verterunt ad me dorsum, et non faciem. Isti æquissimo Dei judicio merentur damnationem æternam.
paras.en: [[1:6|And them that turn away from following after the Lord|Et qui avertuntur de post tergum Domini]], [[1:6|and that have not sought|et qui non quæsierunt]] him. These are they who turn their mind away from God, and prefer their own will to the divine will, and are not ashamed to be ungrateful for all the benefits of their Creator: who do God an irreverence and injury the greater, the more he excels the created, carnal and earthly things which the sinner has chosen for himself in his stead, and the more good things we have received from him, and the more just it is that he be preferred to all. Therefore it is written: [[Ps 118:21|they are cursed who decline from thy commandments|Maledicti qui declinant a mandatis tuis]]; and again, [[Ps 118:118|Thou hast despised all them that fall off from|Sprevisti omnes discedentes]] thy justices [Denis reads *justitiis*, "justices", where the Vulgate has *judiciis*, "judgments"]. Of such the Lord speaks in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:27|they have turned their back to me, and not their face|Verterunt ad me dorsum, et non faciem]]. These, by the most equitable judgment of God, deserve eternal damnation.

paras.t: Silete a facie Domini, id est, ex consideratione divinæ præsentiæ omnia intuentis ac judicantis metuite, atque a verbis præsumptuosis et incautis cessate, quia juxta est dies Domini, id est tempus quo nos visitabit et judicabit, scilicet hora mortis et particularis judicii, vel etiam judicii finalis ac generalis, quod comparatione durationis futuri sæculi, propinquum est valde. Quia præparavit Dominus hostiam, id est, reprobos damnationi et spirituali æternæ occisioni dare disposuit; sanctificavit vocatos suos, puta electos, quemadmodum ad Romanos scribit Apostolus : Quos prædestinavit, hos et vocavit; et quos vocavit, hos et justificavit. Potest quoque per diem Domini, tempus gratiæ, et per hostiam a Deo paratam, Sacramentum altaris intelligi, cui cum omni reverentia, fervore et quiete mentali obviare debemus.
paras.en: [[1:7|Be silent before the face of the Lord|Silete a facie Domini]], that is: from the thought of the divine presence, which beholds and judges all things, be afraid, and cease from presumptuous and careless words; [[1:7|for the day of the Lord is near|quia juxta est dies Domini]], that is, the time in which he will visit and judge us, namely the hour of death and of the particular judgment, or also of the final and general judgment, which, compared with the duration of the world to come, is very near. [[1:7|for the Lord hath prepared a victim|Quia præparavit Dominus hostiam]], that is, he has determined to give over the reprobate to damnation and to eternal spiritual slaughter; [[1:7|he hath sanctified his guests|sanctificavit vocatos suos]] [*vocatos*, literally "his called ones"], namely the elect, as the Apostle writes to the Romans: [[Rom 8:30|whom he predestinated, them he also called. And whom he called, them he also justified|Quos prædestinavit, hos et vocavit; et quos vocavit, hos et justificavit]]. By the day of the Lord can also be understood the time of grace, and by the victim prepared by God the Sacrament of the altar [*hostia*, "victim", is also the word for the Host], which we ought to go to meet with all reverence, fervour and quiet of mind.

paras.t: Et erit : In die hostiæ Domini, id est in extremo judicio seu omni tempore ultionis divinæ, vel quotidie, quando Hostia sacra altaris Deo offertur, visitabo super principes, et super filios regis, id est elatos sæculi dominatores eorumque posteros, magnates et nobiles, qui de sua nobilitate, potentia, opulentia, fama et gloria jactant se ipsos et inaniter gaudent, et subditos opprimunt, non juste gubernant, alios quoque contemnunt. Isti in die judicii simul peribunt : imo quotidie gravissime (quod ipsi non sentiunt) visitantur, dum a Deo juste relinquuntur; itaque indesinenter peccatis peccata adjiciunt, animas suas dilaniant, dæmonibus obsequuntur, et iram Dei sibi miserabiliter thesaurizant. Denique communiter in Scripturis comminatur Dominus principibus ac prælatis. Unde Isaias asserit : Visitabit Dominus super militiam cœli, et super principes terræ. Propterea in libro Sapientiæ ait Scriptura : Præbete aures, vos qui continetis multitudines, quoniam data est vobis a Deo potestas, qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur : quoniam judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet. Hinc in Jeremia Dominus loquitur : Non glorietur fortis in fortitudine sua, et non glorietur dives in divitiis suis.
paras.en: [[1:8|And it shall come to pass in the day of the victim of the Lord|Et erit : In die hostiæ Domini]], that is, at the last judgment, or at every time of divine vengeance, or daily, when the sacred Host of the altar is offered to God, [[1:8|that I will visit upon the princes, and upon the king's sons|visitabo super principes, et super filios regis]], that is, the proud lords of the world and their descendants, the great and the noble, who boast of their nobility, power, wealth, fame and glory and rejoice in vain, and oppress their subjects, do not govern justly, and despise others besides. These will perish together on the day of judgment: nay, daily they are most heavily visited (which they themselves do not feel), while they are justly forsaken by God; and so they unceasingly add sins to sins[[Ecclus 5:5||]], tear their own souls, obey the demons, and wretchedly treasure up for themselves the wrath of God[[Rom 2:5||]]. In short, the Lord commonly threatens princes and prelates in the Scriptures. Hence Isaias declares: [[Is 24:21|the Lord shall visit upon the host of heaven|Visitabit Dominus super militiam cœli]], [[Is 24:21|and upon the kings of the earth|et super principes terræ]] [Denis reads *principes*, "princes", for *reges*, "kings"]. Therefore Scripture says in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 6:3|Give ear, you that rule the people|Præbete aures, vos qui continetis multitudines]], [[Wis 6:4|For power is given you by the Lord|quoniam data est vobis a Deo potestas]], [[Wis 6:4|who will examine your works: and search out your thoughts|qui interrogabit opera vestra, et cogitationes vestras scrutabitur]]: [[Wis 6:6|for a most severe judgment shall be for them that bear rule|quoniam judicium durissimum in his qui præsunt, fiet]]. Hence the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:23|let not the strong man glory in his strength, and let not the rich man glory in his riches|Non glorietur fortis in fortitudine sua, et non glorietur dives in divitiis suis]].

paras.t: Et super omnes qui induti sunt veste peregrina. Hoc verbo reprobantur a Deo, qui in vestibus superstitiosi sunt, et varias novitates vanosque ornatus confingunt; item, qui animæ indumenta negligentes (de quibus dicit Apostolus : Induite viscera misericordiæ, benignitatem, humilitatem, modestiam, patientiam) induunt vestimenta diaboli, passiones et vitia.
paras.en: [[1:8|and upon all such as are clothed with strange apparel|Et super omnes qui induti sunt veste peregrina]]. By this word those are condemned by God who are superstitious about clothes and devise various novelties and vain adornments; likewise those who, neglecting the garments of the soul (of which the Apostle says: [[Col 3:12|Put ye on|Induite]] [[Col 3:12|the bowels of mercy, benignity, humility, modesty, patience|viscera misericordiæ, benignitatem, humilitatem, modestiam, patientiam]]), put on the garments of the devil, passions and vices.

paras.t: Et super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur. Quid enim superbit terra et cinis? Imo odibilis Deo et hominibus est superbia. Ideo in Proverbiorum libro legitur : Abominatio est Domino omnis arrogans. Qui complent domum Dei sui iniquitate et dolo. Hi sunt sacerdotes et clerici qui in ecclesia opus Dei faciunt fraudulenter, et Horas imperfecte cursorieque persolvunt, qui oculis vagi et sensibus incustoditi, menteque vani ac garruli, aliis malum præbent exemplum. Quod et de vulgo accipi potest, scilicet his qui divino Officio indevote et irreverenter adsistunt, et præsertim de his qui in templo Dei sacrisve locis sæcularia atque illicita tractant, emunt, vendunt, vel mulieres adspiciunt. Horum damnatio justa est.
paras.en: [[1:9|upon every one that entereth arrogantly|Et super omnem qui arroganter ingreditur]]. [[Ecclus 10:9|Why is earth, and ashes proud|Quid enim superbit terra et cinis]]? Nay, [[Ecclus 10:7|Pride is hateful before God and men|odibilis Deo et hominibus est superbia]]. Therefore we read in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 16:5|Every proud man is an abomination to the Lord|Abominatio est Domino omnis arrogans]]. [[1:9|them that fill the house of the Lord their God with iniquity and deceit|Qui complent domum Dei sui iniquitate et dolo]]. These are the priests and clerics who in church do the work of God deceitfully[[Jer 48:10||]], and say the Hours incompletely and in haste, who, with wandering eyes and unguarded senses, and vain and chattering minds, give others a bad example. This can also be taken of the common people, namely of those who attend the divine Office without devotion and reverence, and especially of those who in the temple of God or in holy places deal in worldly and unlawful things, buy, sell, or look at women. [[Rom 3:8|Whose damnation is just|Horum damnatio justa est]].

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus, puta in die judicii, vox clamoris a porta Piscium, id est afflictio sensuum exteriorum, qui curiositati frequenter deserviunt : et in Scripturis nomine piscium curiosi aliquando designantur; et ululatus a Secunda, id est tribulatio quantum ad sensus interiores, et contritio magna a collibus, id est grandis calamitas superiorum virium animæ, intellectus et voluntatis. Tunc enim damnandi, in omnibus corporis membris et animæ viribus punientur, tribulabuntur, et ululabunt, juxta illud Sapientiæ : Videntes, turbabuntur timore horribili, præ angustia spiritus gementes.
paras.en: [[1:10|And there shall be in that day, saith the Lord|Et erit in die illa, dicit Dominus]], namely on the day of judgment, [[1:10|the noise of a cry from the fish gate|vox clamoris a porta Piscium]], that is, the affliction of the outward senses, which often serve curiosity: and in the Scriptures the curious are sometimes signified by the name of fishes; [[1:10|and a howling from the Second|et ululatus a Secunda]], that is, tribulation as regards the inward senses, [[1:10|and a great destruction from the hills|et contritio magna a collibus]], that is, a great calamity of the higher powers of the soul, the intellect and the will. For then those who are to be damned will be punished, afflicted and will howl in all the members of the body and the powers of the soul, according to that of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:2|These seeing it, shall be troubled with terrible fear|Videntes, turbabuntur timore horribili]], [[Wis 5:3|groaning for anguish of spirit|præ angustia spiritus gementes]].

paras.t: Ululate, habitatores pilæ. Per pilam (quæ sicut prædictum est, vas quoddam quo grana tunduntur) hoc loco intelligi potest caro nostra mortalis, de qua dicit Apostolus, Sciat unusquisque possidere vas suum in sanctificatione : quæ nunc diversis tribulationibus est subjecta. Hujus pilæ habitatores proprie appellantur, qui carnem suam non spiritualiter, sed carnaliter diligunt, curam carnis in desideriis perficientes, atque in carne carnaliter conversantes. Istis nunc flendum est pœnitentiæ lacrimis : quod nisi peregerint, in die judicii sui ululabunt. Qui autem carnem spiritui subdunt, dicuntur non esse in carne. Unde ad Romanos dicit Apostolus : Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt. Vos autem, inquit, in carne non estis, sed in spiritu. Insuper omnibus nobis in hac lacrimarum valle mortalique carne (quæ per pilam intelligi potest) morantibus, flendum est atque gemendum pro propriis ac aliorum peccatis, pro patriæ dilatione, ex fame et siti justitiæ, ex Christi compassione.
paras.en: [[1:11|Howl, ye inhabitants of the Morter|Ululate, habitatores pilæ]]. By the *mortar* (which, as was said before, is a vessel in which grain is pounded) can be understood in this place our mortal flesh, of which the Apostle says, [[1 Thess 4:4|every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification|Sciat unusquisque possidere vas suum in sanctificatione]]: which is now subject to divers tribulations. Those are properly called inhabitants of this mortar who love their flesh not spiritually but carnally, fulfilling the care of the flesh in its desires, and living carnally in the flesh. These must weep now with tears of penance: and unless they do so, they will howl on the day of their judgment. But those who subject the flesh to the spirit are said not to be in the flesh. Hence the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 8:8|they who are in the flesh cannot please God|Qui in carne sunt, Deo placere non possunt]]. [[Rom 8:9|But you|Vos autem]], he says, [[Rom 8:9|are not in the flesh, but the spirit|in carne non estis, sed in spiritu]]. Moreover, all of us who dwell in this valley of tears and in mortal flesh (which can be understood by the mortar) must weep and groan for our own sins and those of others, for the delay of our homeland, out of hunger and thirst for justice, and out of compassion for Christ.

paras.t: Conticuit, id est, Deo in die judicii respondere non poterit, et in vita præsenti a laudibus Dei obmutuit, omnis populus Chanaan, id est plebs omnis instabilis, quæ omni vento doctrinæ et impetu passionum circumfertur, variisque cogitationibus atque affectibus contra justitiam agitatur. Propter quod primo Regum habetur : Impii in tenebris conticescent. Chanaan equidem interpretatur commotio. Ideo ad Corinthios hortatur Apostolus : Fratres mei, stabiles estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper, scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino. Hinc Christus hominem verbis Dei non obedientem, comparat viro stulto qui ædificavit domum suam super arenam, cujus ruina facta est magna. Disperierunt omnes involuti argento, videlicet divites sæculi hujus et cupidi. Omnium quippe malorum radix est cupiditas, teste Apostolo : qui avaritiam quoque idololatriam vocat; et ad Timotheum contestatur, Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli. Eapropter scriptum est in Baruch : Ubi sunt qui thesaurizant argentum et aurum, et non est finis possessionis eorum? Exterminati sunt, et ad inferos descenderunt; viam autem disciplinæ ignoraverunt.
paras.en: [[1:11|is hush|Conticuit]], that is, will not be able to answer God on the day of judgment, and in the present life has fallen dumb from the praises of God, [[1:11|All the people of Chanaan|omnis populus Chanaan]], that is, every unstable people, which is carried about by every wind of doctrine[[Eph 4:14||]] and by the onset of the passions, and is tossed by various thoughts and affections against justice. Wherefore it is found in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:9|the wicked shall be silent in darkness|Impii in tenebris conticescent]]. For *Chanaan* is interpreted *commotion*. Therefore the Apostle exhorts the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:58|my beloved brethren, be ye steadfast and unmoveable: always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labour is not in vain in the Lord|Fratres mei, stabiles estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper, scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino]]. Hence Christ compares the man who does not obey the words of God to a foolish man that built his house upon the sand[[Matt 7:26||]], whose fall was great[[Matt 7:27||]]. [[1:11|all are cut off that were wrapped up in silver|Disperierunt omnes involuti argento]], namely the rich of this world and the covetous. For [[1 Tim 6:10|the desire of money is the root of all evils|Omnium quippe malorum radix est cupiditas]], as the Apostle testifies: who also calls avarice idolatry[[Eph 5:5||]][[Col 3:5||]]; and he solemnly tells Timothy, [[1 Tim 6:9|they that will become rich fall into temptation and into the snare of the devil|Qui volunt divites fieri, incidunt in tentationem et laqueum diaboli]]. Therefore it is written in Baruch: [[Bar 3:16|Where are|Ubi sunt]] they [[Bar 3:18|That hoard up silver and gold|qui thesaurizant argentum et aurum]], [[Bar 3:18|and there is no end of their getting|et non est finis possessionis eorum]]? [[Bar 3:19|They are cut off, and are gone down to hell|Exterminati sunt, et ad inferos descenderunt]]; [[Bar 3:20|but the way of knowledge they have not known|viam autem disciplinæ ignoraverunt]].

paras.t: Et erit in tempore illo judicii generalis et etiam particularis : Scrutabor ego Unigenitus Dei Jesus Christus, qui sum judex et testis, cui Pater dedit omne judicium, Jerusalem, id est Ecclesiam animamque credentem, in lucernis, id est in libris conscientiæ, de quibus in Daniele et Apocalypsi scriptum est : Aperti sunt libri. Vel, In lucernis, id est lumine veritatis et sacræ Scripturæ sermonibus, examinabo opera ejus. Nihil enim opertum, quod non revelabitur; et quum venerit Dominus, illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium. Potest quoque interpretari in bono, ut in præsenti Deus electorum suorum vitam dicatur in lucernis scrutari, quando per prælatos ac judices, sapientes ac virtuosos (qui sunt lucernæ lucentes et ardentes), examinat, castigat atque emendat subjectos ; vel certe dum unicuique dat gratiam illustrationis supernæ, qua se ipsum digne examinat, judicat, corrigit et gubernat. Et visitabo super viros defixos in fœcibus suis, id est, qui mentem suam ad superna non elevant, sed concupiscentiis turpissimis obtenebrati, indurantur in vitiis ; qui dicunt, Non faciet Dominus bene, et non faciet male, id est, divinam providentiam negant, vel formaliter et directe, vel æquivalenter et indirecte : quia sic vivunt, quasi non esset Deus humanorum actuum judex, dum sine timore perpetrant mala, nec metuendum Dei pensant judicium. Propter quod fides eorum mortua perhibetur. Non enim habent hujusmodi fidem de qua scribit apostolus Joannes : Hæc est victoria quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra; et in Marco dicitur, Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit.
paras.en: [[1:12|And it shall come to pass at that time|Et erit in tempore illo]] of the general and also of the particular judgment: [[1:12|I will search|Scrutabor]], I, the Only-begotten of God, Jesus Christ, who am [[Jer 29:23|the judge and the witness|judex et testis]], to whom the Father [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment|dedit omne judicium]], [[1:12|Jerusalem|Jerusalem]], that is, the Church and the believing soul, [[1:12|with lamps|in lucernis]], that is, in the books of conscience, of which it is written in Daniel and the Apocalypse: [[Dan 7:10|the books were opened|Aperti sunt libri]][[Apoc 20:12||]]. Or, *with lamps*, that is, by the light of truth and the words of sacred Scripture, I will examine its works. For [[Matt 10:26|nothing is covered that shall not be revealed|Nihil enim opertum, quod non revelabitur]]; and [[1 Cor 4:5|until the Lord come|quum venerit Dominus]], he [[1 Cor 4:5|will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts|illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum, et manifestabit consilia cordium]]. This can also be interpreted in a good sense, so that God may be said in the present to search the life of his elect with lamps, when through prelates and judges who are wise and virtuous (who are burning and shining lamps[[John 5:35||]]) he examines, chastises and corrects those under them; or surely when he gives to each one the grace of heavenly enlightenment, by which he worthily examines, judges, corrects and governs himself. [[1:12|and will visit upon the men that are settled on their lees|Et visitabo super viros defixos in fœcibus suis]], that is, those who do not lift their mind to things above, but, darkened by the foulest lusts, are hardened in vices; [[1:12|that say|qui dicunt]], [[1:12|The Lord will not do good, nor will he do evil|Non faciet Dominus bene, et non faciet male]], that is, they deny divine providence, either formally and directly, or equivalently and indirectly: for they live as if God were not the judge of human acts, while they [[Eccles 8:11|commit evils without any fear|sine timore perpetrant mala]] and do not weigh the judgment of God, which is to be feared. For this reason their faith is said to be dead. For they do not have such faith as the apostle John writes of: [[1 John 5:4|this is the victory which overcameth the world: Our faith|Hæc est victoria quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra]]; and in Mark it is said, [[Mark 16:16|He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved|Qui crediderit et baptizatus fuerit, salvus erit]].

paras.t: Et erit fortitudo eorum in direptionem, id est, hostibus suis tradentur torquendi, et nunc dæmonum prædæ sunt, et ab inferno deglutientur, et domus eorum in desertum, quia corda eorum deserentur a Deo, atque æternæ oblivioni tradentur. Hæc enim sunt domus sive cubilia de quibus cantatur : In cubilibus vestris compungimini. Vel per domos corpora designantur, quæ post mortem in pulverem rediguntur. Et ædificabunt domos, et non inhabitabunt; et plantabunt vineas, et non bibent vinum earum. Reprobi quippe et sapientes hujus mundi, in quibus dominatur prudentia carnis, quæ mors animæ est, secundum Apostolum, nunc colligunt sibi terrena et construunt, quasi diu victuri; et frequenter, dum non suspicantur, tolluntur de medio, nec uti suis divitiis permittuntur. Secundum quod, diviti qui dicebat, Anima, habes reposita multa bona in annos plurimos, requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare; divinitus respondetur : Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te ; quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt? Hinc ait Psalmista : Verumtamen in imagine pertransit homo, sed et frustra conturbatur; thesaurizat, et ignorat cui congregabit ea.
paras.en: [[1:13|And their strength shall become a booty|Et erit fortitudo eorum in direptionem]], that is, they will be handed over to their enemies to be tormented, and are now the prey of demons, and will be swallowed up by hell; [[1:13|and their houses as a desert|et domus eorum in desertum]], because their hearts will be forsaken by God and given over to eternal oblivion. For these are the houses or chambers of which it is sung: [[Ps 4:5|be sorry for them upon your beds|In cubilibus vestris compungimini]] [*cubilia*, "chambers" or "beds"]. Or by the houses are signified bodies, which after death are reduced to dust. [[1:13|and they shall build houses, and shall not dwell in them: and they shall plant vineyards, and shall not drink the wine of them|Et ædificabunt domos, et non inhabitabunt; et plantabunt vineas, et non bibent vinum earum]]. For the reprobate and the wise of this world, in whom reigns [[Rom 8:6|the wisdom of the flesh|prudentia carnis]], which is the death of the soul, according to the Apostle, now gather and build up earthly things for themselves, as if they were to live long; and often, when they do not suspect it, they are taken from the midst and not allowed to use their riches. In accordance with which, to the rich man who said, [[Luke 12:19|Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years. Take thy rest: eat, drink, make good cheer|Anima, habes reposita multa bona in annos plurimos, requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare]], answer is made from God: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee. And whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetunt a te ; quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt?]]? Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 38:7|Surely man passeth as an image: yea, and he is disquieted in vain. He storeth up: and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things|Verumtamen in imagine pertransit homo, sed et frustra conturbatur; thesaurizat, et ignorat cui congregabit ea]].

paras.t: Juxta est dies Domini magnus et velox nimis. Non mirum est hoc de die novissimo dici, quum Joannes in prima sua ferat Canonica : Novissima hora est. Et Paulus : Nos, inquit, sumus, in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt; itemque : Adhuc modicum, et qui venturus est, veniet. Vox diei Domini amara. Nonne damnandis amarissima erit vox illa, Surgite, mortui, venite ad judicium; et, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum? Tribulabitur ibi fortis, id est potentes sua potentia abutentes, qui vere infirmi sunt, quoniam diabolo, mundo, et suæ carni succumbunt atque deserviunt. Verumtamen potentes Deus non abjicit, quum ipse sit potens, dummodo viribus sibi concessis juste utantur.
paras.en: [[1:14|The great day of the Lord is near|Juxta est dies Domini magnus]] [[1:14|and exceeding swift|et velox nimis]]. It is no wonder that this is said of the last day, since John declares in his first Canonical epistle [[1 John 2:18|that it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]]. And Paul: We, he says, are they [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]]; and again: [[Heb 10:37|yet a little|Adhuc modicum]], [[Heb 10:37|and he that is to come will come|et qui venturus est, veniet]]. [[1:14|the voice of the day of the Lord is bitter|Vox diei Domini amara]]. Will not that voice be most bitter to those who are to be damned: Arise, ye dead, come to judgment; and, Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]? [[1:14|the mighty man shall there meet with tribulation|Tribulabitur ibi fortis]], that is, the powerful who abuse their power, who are truly weak, since they give way to and serve the devil, the world and their own flesh. Yet [[Job 36:5|God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty|potentes Deus non abjicit, quum ipse sit potens]], provided they use justly the strength granted them.

paras.t: Dies iræ dies illa, dies tribulationis et angustiæ, dies calamitatis et miseriæ; dies tenebrarum et caliginis, de quo ait Psalmista, Nubes et caligo in circuitu ejus; dies nebulæ et turbinis, secundum illud in Psalmo, Ignis in conspectu ejus exardescet, et in circuitu ejus tempestas valida; dies tubæ et clangoris : dicit enim Apostolus ad Thessalonicenses, Quoniam ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce archangeli et in tuba Dei descendet de cœlo; et iterum, In momento, in ictu oculi, in novissima tuba resurgemus, canet enim tuba; super civitates munitas, id est congregationes bonis hujus mundi vallatas, et angulos excelsos, id est superiores, ad quos velut ad angulos confugiunt alii.
